newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks skid to lower close, properties rocked.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks skid to lower close, properties rocked.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks skidded to a sharply lower close on Thursday after a government move to curb soaring real estate prices rocked property counters.
The Hang Seng Index tumbled 242.07 points, or 1.89 percent, to 12,534.32. Turnover was HK$8.96 billion compared with HK$7.27 billion on Wednesday.
"I think the market is very concerned about possible further action to stop property speculation and increase supply," said Miles Remington, a sales trader at SocGen-Crosby Securities.
The government said on Wednesday it would extend the presale period for private flats to bring more supply to the market.

"People have no idea what will happen between the property developers and the government," said Sunny Chan, senior research manager at Seapower Securities. "Today is the last day before the holiday so no one wants to buy."
The stock market is closed on Friday and Monday for the Easter holiday. Over the abbreviated four-day week, the index rose 45.02 points or 0.36 percent.
Shares in Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd slumped HK$2.25 to HK$68.25 and Sun Hung Kai Properties Ltd fell HK$3.25 to HK$82.00.
Henderson Land Development Co Ltd slid HK$2.50 to HK$64.25 and New World Development Co Ltd dropped HK$1.70 to HK$41.80.

The government also said on Wednesday that developers would have to put presale flats onto the market within six months of the date of consent and release a "reasonable quantity" each time -- no less than 20 percent of every batch.
"This may not give property developers much space for the selling schedule," said Chan.
He expected the sector to remain the focus next week and the market could face further downward pressure, with a trading range of 12,300 to 12,700 points for the Hang Seng Index.
Futures finished at a steep discount to the cash market with April Hang Seng Index futures ending down 242 points at 12,458.
Hutchison Whampoa Ltd made gains despite the market's fall. The Hong Kong conglomerate posted a 25.6 percent rise in 1996 net profit to HK$12.02 billion on Wednesday.
Shares in HSBC Holdings Plc fell HK$1.50 to HK$180.00 and Hang Seng Bank Ltd fell HK$1.93 to HK$80.00.
Television Broadcasts Ltd rose HK$0.20 to HK$31.50. The company reported 1996 net profit of HK$477.20 million on Wednesday compared with HK$485.55 million for 1995.
GITIC Enterprises Ltd fell HK$0.50 to HK$3.875 after making a strong market debut on Wednesday.
